title: Vous + present tense
subtitle: Using the polite/plural you form
explanation: Use vous with many present tense verbs. In Course 8, vous is used for you eat, you are, and many polite questions.

examples.eng: you eat / you're eating
examples.fre: vous mangez

examples.eng: you are
examples.fre: vous êtes

examples.eng: you have I
examples.fre: vous avez

title: Ne ... pas
subtitle: Making a sentence negative
explanation: Put ne before the verb and pas after it to say not. With vous forms, this gives patterns like vous ne mangez pas.

examples.eng: you don't eat / you're not eating
examples.fre: vous ne mangez pas

examples.eng: don't you eat? / aren't you eating?
examples.fre: ne mangez-vous pas?

examples.eng: don't eat!
examples.fre: ne mangez pas!

title: Inversion questions
subtitle: Asking by reversing verb and subject
explanation: French can ask questions by putting the verb before the subject with a hyphen. Course 8 uses this in questions like mangez-vous and va-t-elle.

examples.eng: do you eat? / are you eating?
examples.fre: mangez-vous?

examples.eng: Whom do you like?
examples.fre: Qui aimes-tu? / Qui aimez-vous?

examples.eng: What are you eating?
examples.fre: Que mangez-vous?

title: Negative questions
subtitle: Asking don’t you / aren’t you
explanation: Use ne before the verb and pas after the subject-verb question form to ask a negative question.

examples.eng: don't you eat? / aren't you eating?
examples.fre: ne mangez-vous pas?

examples.eng: Why don't you like this hôtel?
examples.fre: Pourquoi n'aimez-vous pas cet hôtel?

examples.eng: don't pa?
examples.fre: je ne paye pas

title: Imperatives
subtitle: Giving commands
explanation: Use the command form to tell someone to do something. Course 8 uses short commands like Mangez and Faites.

examples.eng: don't eat!
examples.fre: ne mangez pas!

examples.eng: Eat!
examples.fre: Mangez!

examples.eng: Do everything tomorrow!
examples.fre: Faites tout demain!

title: Soyez
subtitle: Saying be as a command
explanation: Soyez is the polite/plural command form of être. Use it to say be in instructions.

examples.eng: Please be patient.
examples.fre: Veuillez patienter.

examples.eng: Please be patient; I'm coming now
examples.fre: patienter, je viens maintenant

title: Veuillez
subtitle: Polite instructions
explanation: Veuillez makes a request sound formal and polite, like please do this.

examples.eng: Please, wait here
examples.fre: Veuillez attendre ici

examples.eng: please (be so kind as to...
examples.fre: veuillez

examples.eng: Please, come in.
examples.fre: Veuillez entrer.

title: ER verbs in the present
subtitle: Je forms of regular ER verbs
explanation: For many ER verbs, the je form ends in -e. Course 8 uses je mange, je parle, je donne, and similar forms.

examples.eng: eat / I'I'm eating
examples.fre: je mange

examples.eng: I speak / I'm speaking
examples.fre: je parle

examples.eng: I give / I'm giving
examples.fre: je donne

title: Infinitives
subtitle: The dictionary form of a verb
explanation: Infinitives are the basic to form of a verb, such as manger, parler, and donner.

examples.eng: to eat
examples.fre: manger

examples.eng: to speak
examples.fre: parler

examples.eng: to give
examples.fre: donner

title: Je + present tense
subtitle: Saying I do / I am doing
explanation: The present tense can mean both I do and I am doing in French. Je mange can mean I eat or I am eating.

examples.eng: eat / I'I'm eating
examples.fre: je mange

examples.eng: I speak / I'm speaking
examples.fre: je parle

examples.eng: dance / I'm dancing
examples.fre: je danse

title: Quand
subtitle: Using when
explanation: Use quand to connect an action with when something happens.

examples.eng: I spend too much money when I go on holiday.
examples.fre: Je dépense trop d'argent quand je vais en vacances.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

examples.eng: I eat lots of cheese when I go to France.
examples.fre: Je mange beaucoup de fromage quand je vais en France.

title: Parce que
subtitle: Using because
explanation: Use parce que to give a reason.

examples.eng: I'm changing rooms because there is no shower in this room.
examples.fre: Je change de chambre parce qu'il n'y a pas de douche dans cette chambre.

examples.eng: I'm trying to understand but it's difficult because you're not speaking very slowly.
examples.fre: J'essaye de comprendre mais c'est difficile parce que vous ne parlez pas très lentement.

examples.eng: I gain weight when I go on holiday because I eat too many ice-creams.
examples.fre: Je grossis quand je vais en vacances parce que je mange trop de glaces.

title: Chez
subtitle: Saying at someone’s place
explanation: Use chez to mean at the house/place of a person or business.

examples.eng: I'm bringing some food to your house tonight.
examples.fre: J'apporte de la nourriture chez vous ce soir.

examples.eng: I visit my grandma at her house every Thursday evening.
examples.fre: Je visite ma grandmère chez elle tous les jeudis soir.

examples.eng: I'm staying at home tonight; I'm very tired
examples.fre: Je reste chez moi ce soir; je suis très fatigué

title: IR verbs
subtitle: Regular IR verb patterns
explanation: Course 8 introduces IR verbs such as finir and choisir. These verbs use forms like je finis and nous finissons.

examples.eng: to finish
examples.fre: je finis

examples.eng: to finish
examples.fre: finir

examples.eng: to choose
examples.fre: choisir

title: Faire
subtitle: Using faire
explanation: Faire means to do or to make. It appears in commands and everyday actions.

examples.eng: Do everything tomorrow!
examples.fre: Faites tout demain!

examples.eng: to make
examples.fre: je fais

examples.eng: to do / to make
examples.fre: faire

title: Dire
subtitle: Using dire
explanation: Dire means to say or to tell. It is used with messages and reporting information.

examples.eng: I visit my grandma at her house every Thursday evening.
examples.fre: Je visite ma grandmère chez elle tous les jeudis soir.

examples.eng: Every Tuesday, I finish at twelve o'clock.
examples.fre: Tous les mardis, je finis à douze heures.

examples.eng: to say / to tell
examples.fre: dire

title: Boire
subtitle: Using boire
explanation: Boire means to drink. Course 8 uses it for drinks and dinner situations.

examples.eng: to drink
examples.fre: boire

examples.eng: 1 drink / I'm drinking
examples.fre: je bois

examples.eng: I'm drinking red wine with dinner.
examples.fre: Je bois du vin rouge avec le dîner.

title: Prendre
subtitle: Using prendre
explanation: Prendre means to take. It can also appear in useful expressions like taking lunch or taking a taxi.

examples.eng: I'm trying to understand but it's difficult because you're not speaking very slowly.
examples.fre: J'essaye de comprendre mais c'est difficile parce que vous ne parlez pas très lentement.

examples.eng: I'm trying to learn French and I'm
examples.fre: J'essaye d'apprendre le français et je réussis.

examples.eng: to take
examples.fre: prendre

title: Avoir
subtitle: Using avoir
explanation: Avoir means to have. Course 8 uses it in present-tense forms like j’ai, tu as, and ils ont.

examples.eng: I'm going to have dinner here
examples.fre: Je vais prendre le dîner ici

examples.eng: We're going to have dinner here on Sunday
examples.fre: Nous allons prendre le dîner ici dimanche

examples.eng: Do you have any bags?
examples.fre: Avez-vous des sacs?

title: Être
subtitle: Using être
explanation: Être means to be. Course 8 uses forms like je suis, vous êtes, and ils sont.

examples.eng: you are
examples.fre: vous êtes

examples.eng: I'm staying at home tonight; I'm very tired
examples.fre: Je reste chez moi ce soir; je suis très fatigué

examples.eng: I am I come
examples.fre: je suis je viens I

title: Aller
subtitle: Using aller
explanation: Aller means to go. It is also used to build near-future sentences with another verb.

examples.eng: I spend too much money when I go on holiday.
examples.fre: Je dépense trop d'argent quand je vais en vacances.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

examples.eng: I eat lots of cheese when I go to France.
examples.fre: Je mange beaucoup de fromage quand je vais en France.

title: Near future: aller + infinitive
subtitle: Saying going to do something
explanation: Use aller plus an infinitive to say that someone is going to do something.

examples.eng: I'm going to have dinner here
examples.fre: Je vais prendre le dîner ici

examples.eng: We're going to have dinner here on Sunday
examples.fre: Nous allons prendre le dîner ici dimanche

examples.eng: I'm going to Sophie's house now.
examples.fre: Je vais chez Sophie maintenant.

title: Depuis
subtitle: Saying for/since with ongoing actions
explanation: Use depuis when something started earlier and is still true now.

examples.eng: I've been waiting here for an hour.
examples.fre: J'attends ici depuis une heure.

examples.eng: I haven't been waiting long.
examples.fre: Je n'attends pas depuis longtemps.

title: Direct object pronouns
subtitle: Using le, la, les before a verb
explanation: Le, la, and les can replace a thing or person already mentioned. Course 8 uses forms like le laisser and l’acheter.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

examples.eng: I'm choosing something for lunch.
examples.fre: Je choisis quelque chose pour le déjeuner.

examples.eng: I'm trying to learn French and I'm
examples.fre: J'essaye d'apprendre le français et je réussis.

title: Indirect object pronouns
subtitle: Using me, te, lui, nous, vous, leur
explanation: Indirect object pronouns show to me, to you, to him/her, to us, to you, or to them.

examples.eng: Hello and welcome
examples.fre: Bonjour et bienvenue

examples.eng: Please, come in.
examples.fre: Veuillez entrer.

examples.eng: I'm bringing some food to your house tonight.
examples.fre: J'apporte de la nourriture chez vous ce soir.

title: Pronouns with commands
subtitle: Putting pronouns after commands
explanation: In positive commands, pronouns often come after the verb with a hyphen, such as montre-moi.

examples.eng: Excuse me, what time is it?
examples.fre: Excusez-moi, quelle heure est-il?

examples.eng: leave me here
examples.fre: laisse-moi ici / laissez-moi ici

examples.eng: listen to me
examples.fre: écoute-moi / écoutez-moi

title: Ne ... pas with pronouns
subtitle: Negating sentences with object pronouns
explanation: When a pronoun is used, it usually stays before the verb, and ne...pas wraps around that verb group.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

examples.eng: I'm spending two weeks in Spain next year
examples.fre: Je passe deux semaines en Espagne l'année

examples.eng: I'm not calling Pierre; I don't like him.
examples.fre: Je n'appelle pas Pierre; je ne l'aime pas.

title: Passé composé with avoir
subtitle: Talking about completed past actions
explanation: Use avoir plus a past participle to talk about many completed past actions.

examples.eng: I'm spending a month in Paris next year.
examples.fre: Je passe un mois à Paris l'année prochaine.

examples.eng: I'm visiting my family abroad soon.
examples.fre: Je visite ma famille à l'étranger bientôt.

examples.eng: I'm not trying any cheese; I've eaten too much today.
examples.fre: Je n'essaye pas de fromage; j'ai trop mangé aujourd'hui.

title: Passé composé with être
subtitle: Past actions with movement verbs
explanation: Some movement verbs use être in the passé composé, such as aller and partir.

examples.eng: I wonder where.
examples.fre: Je me demande où elle est allée.

examples.eng: A bottle of water is one euro twenty
examples.fre: Une bouteille d'eau est un euro vingt

examples.eng: There wasn't much to do when I went on holiday to La Rochelle.
examples.fre: ll n'y avait pas beaucoup à faire quand je suis allé en vacances à La OO

title: Past-tense questions
subtitle: Asking about completed actions
explanation: In the passé composé, questions can use inversion with the helper verb, such as avez-vous or ont-ils.

examples.eng: Why did you try to call me?
examples.fre: Pourquoi as-tu essayé de m'appeler? / Pourquoi avez-vous essayé de m'appeler?

examples.eng: he hasn't given
examples.fre: il n'a pas donné he didn't give

examples.eng: has he given?
examples.fre: a-t-il donné?

title: Devoir + infinitive
subtitle: Saying must / have to
explanation: Use devoir before another verb to say must or have to.

examples.eng: to have to go
examples.fre: être I

examples.eng: I have too many things to do
examples.fre: J'ai trop de choses à faire

examples.eng: I must / I have to
examples.fre: je dois

title: Pouvoir / Puis-je
subtitle: Saying can / may
explanation: Use pouvoir to say can. Puis-je is a polite way to ask may I or can I.

examples.eng: Can you call me tomorrow?
examples.fre: Pouvez-vous m'appeler demain?

examples.eng: I'm busy now, but you can call me after 5pm.
examples.fre: Je suis occupé maintenant, mais vous pouvez m'appeler après dix-sept heures.

examples.eng: I wonder if you can help me.
examples.fre: Je me demande si tu peux m'aider. / Je me demande si vous pouvez m'aider.

title: Vouloir + infinitive
subtitle: Saying want to
explanation: Use vouloir before another verb to say want to do something.

examples.eng: I'm selling my car because I want to change it.
examples.fre: Je vends ma voiture parce que je veux la

examples.eng: I'm selling my car, do you want to buy it?
examples.fre: Je vends ma voiture, voulez-vous l'acheter?

examples.eng: Where do you want to go tonight?
examples.fre: Où voulez-vous aller ce soir?

title: Question words
subtitle: Using what, where, when, why, how
explanation: Course 8 uses question words such as que, où, quand, pourquoi, and combien.

examples.eng: I spend too much money when I go on holiday.
examples.fre: Je dépense trop d'argent quand je vais en vacances.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

examples.eng: I eat lots of cheese when I go to France.
examples.fre: Je mange beaucoup de fromage quand je vais en France.

title: Time expressions
subtitle: Talking about time
explanation: Use à with clock times and phrases like heures, et demie, et quart, and moins le quart.

examples.eng: I start at fI've o'clock today.
examples.fre: Je commence à cinq heures aujourd'hui.

examples.eng: Every Tuesday, I finish at twelve o'clock.
examples.fre: Tous les mardis, je finis à douze heures.

examples.eng: I would like breakfast at nine o'clock
examples.fre: Je voudrais le petit-déjeuner à neuf heures

title: Dans
subtitle: Saying in for future time
explanation: Use dans to say something will happen in a certain amount of time, such as in two weeks.

examples.eng: I'm changing rooms because there is no shower in this room.
examples.fre: Je change de chambre parce qu'il n'y a pas de douche dans cette chambre.

examples.eng: I'm not staying here; there are too many cockroaches in my room.
examples.fre: Je ne reste pas ici; il y a trop de cafards dans ma chambre.

examples.eng: I'm driving there in Marco's car.
examples.fre: Je conduis la dans la voiture de Marco.

title: Demonstratives: ce/cet/cette/ces
subtitle: Saying this/that/these/those
explanation: French demonstratives change with the noun: ce, cet, cette, and ces.

examples.eng: to dance
examples.fre: danser

examples.eng: dance / I'm dancing
examples.fre: je danse

examples.eng: I'm starting tomorrow.
examples.fre: Je commence demain.

title: Possessive adjectives
subtitle: Saying my/your/his/her/our
explanation: Words like mon, ma, mes, votre, and notre show possession.

examples.eng: I'm visiting my family abroad soon.
examples.fre: Je visite ma famille à l'étranger bientôt.

examples.eng: I visit my grandma at her house every Thursday evening.
examples.fre: Je visite ma grandmère chez elle tous les jeudis soir.

examples.eng: I'm choosing a souvenir for my brother.
examples.fre: Je choisis un souvenir pour mon frère.

title: Articles and nouns
subtitle: Using le, la, les, un, une
explanation: Course 8 continues using articles before nouns. Articles often show whether a noun is masculine, feminine, singular, or plural.

examples.eng: I'm bringing some food to your house tonight.
examples.fre: J'apporte de la nourriture chez vous ce soir.

examples.eng: I'm spending a month in Paris next year.
examples.fre: Je passe un mois à Paris l'année prochaine.

examples.eng: I'm hiring a car when we go to Spain next month.
examples.fre: Je loue une voiture quand je vais en Espagne le mois prochain.

title: Prepositions à and de
subtitle: Using to/at/from/of
explanation: À often means to or at, while de can mean of or from. Course 8 uses both in common travel and daily-life phrases.

examples.eng: I start at fI've o'clock today.
examples.fre: Je commence à cinq heures aujourd'hui.

examples.eng: I'm bringing some food to your house tonight.
examples.fre: J'apporte de la nourriture chez vous ce soir.

examples.eng: I'm spending a month in Paris next year.
examples.fre: Je passe un mois à Paris l'année prochaine.
